protection.description: Protects the videos against downloading: their streaming segments are encrypted (AES-128) and the keys are served only to playback tokens and authorized users, at playback pace, to a limited number of simultaneous streams per viewer. The original file cannot be downloaded without nexo:DownloadProtectedMedia, and the Nexo player draws a watermark of the viewer.

protection.prefixHint: Only the keys under this prefix; empty for the whole bucket.
protection.sessionsHint: From 1 to 100; a further stream is refused.
protection.originsHint: Websites allowed to embed the player and fetch the keys, such as https://learn.example.com; any when empty. Press Enter after each one.
protection.watermarkHint: The Nexo player draws the name of the viewer over the video.
protection.shareLinks: Share links play the protected videos
protection.shareLinksHint: Stream share links and presigned playlists play them, without watermark or stream limit.
protection.ttlHint: Longest validity of a playback token, from 1 to 1440 minutes (24 hours); 120 by default.
protection.paceHint: Keys are served at most this many times faster than playback, from 1 to 20; 2 by default.

issues.prefixReserved: The prefix .nexo-media/ is reserved for the outputs.
issues.origin: Each origin must be http(s)://host[:port], without a path.

bucketReplication.unavailable: You cannot read the replication of this bucket.
bucketReplication.targetsDescription: Remote buckets, on Nexo or another S3 server, this bucket can replicate to. Their credentials are stored sealed and never shown again; the remote bucket needs versioning.
bucketReplication.targetsUnavailable: You cannot read the replication targets of this bucket.
bucketReplication.deleteTargetConfirm: Remove the target {{name}} and its stored credentials? What was already replicated stays on the remote bucket.
bucketReplication.endpointHint: URL of the remote S3 API: http(s)://host[:port].
bucketReplication.remoteBucketHint: It must exist and have versioning enabled.
bucketReplication.secretHint: Stored sealed; it is never returned.
bucketReplication.secretKeepHint: Leave empty to keep the stored one.
bucketReplication.label: Label
bucketReplication.rulesDescription: Each new version a rule selects is copied to its target in the background, with its version ID, time and ETag; failures are retried. Versioning cannot be suspended while rules exist.
bucketReplication.noRules: No rule: this bucket is not replicated.
bucketReplication.deleteRuleConfirm: Remove the rule {{id}}? The versions it selects are no longer replicated; what was already replicated stays.
bucketReplication.priorityHint: When several rules select a key for the same target, the highest priority applies.
bucketReplication.priorityInvalid: Enter a whole number, 0 or more.
bucketReplication.tagsHint: key=value entries the objects must all have. Press Enter after each one.
bucketReplication.deleteMarkersHint: A deletion without version ID hides the object on the target too.
bucketReplication.deletesHint: Deleting a version deletes it on the target too.
bucketReplication.existingHint: A resync sends the versions written before the rule.
bucketReplication.activeActive: For an active-active setup, replicate the bucket of each side to the other: replicas are never sent back and the most recent version of a key wins on both sides.
bucketReplication.statusDescription: Versions waiting, replicated and failed for each target since the server started.
bucketReplication.resyncHint: Send the versions written before the rules that the target does not have.
bucketReplication.resyncNeedsExisting: No rule of this target replicates the existing objects.

resyncStates.running: Resync to {{target}} running: {{scanned}} versions scanned, {{queued}} queued.
resyncStates.complete: Resync to {{target}} complete: {{scanned}} versions scanned, {{queued}} queued.
resyncStates.failed: Resync to {{target}} failed after {{scanned}} versions scanned.

bucketReplication.perNode: In a cluster the counters are those of the node that answered.

objectMedia.none: The media worker has not processed this object: no rule selected it, or it is queued.
objectMedia.staleHint: The outputs derive from an older content of this object: they are not used until it is processed again.
objectMedia.queued: The object is queued for processing.
objectMedia.alphaHint: The image has transparency: its JPEG variants are flattened, so browsers that take neither AVIF nor WebP get PNG.
objectMedia.copyVariant: Copy the URL of the {{format}} variant {{resolution}}
objectMedia.variantsHint: These URLs need a console session: to give the image to others, share it with an image link.

subtitles.title: Subtitles
subtitles.none: No subtitles. Upload a WebVTT or SubRip file, or add "subtitles" to the media rule to transcribe the speech.
subtitles.hint: The subtitles play as captions in the console, the player page and every HLS player of the distributions.
subtitles.languageHint: A BCP 47 tag: it, en, pt-BR...
subtitles.fileHint: WebVTT (.vtt) or SubRip (.srt), at most 2 MiB. It replaces the track of that language.
subtitles.tooLarge: The file is larger than 2 MiB.
subtitles.removeManual: Remove the {{name}} subtitles? The track cannot be recovered unless the bucket keeps versions.
subtitles.removeAutomatic: Remove the automatic {{name}} subtitles? They come back when the video is processed again.
subtitles.editAutomatic: This track was made by the media worker: once saved it becomes a manual track, which the worker never overwrites.

problem.order: The cue must end after it starts.
problem.long: The text is longer than 2048 bytes.

siteReplication.title: Site replication
siteReplication.subtitle: Deployments grouped with this one keep their users, groups, access keys, policies and buckets in sync, and every bucket replicates its objects to the same bucket of the other sites. The sites must share the root credentials.
siteReplication.none: This deployment is in no site replication group.
siteReplication.addHint: The first site is this deployment. Every site must be reachable from the others at its Admin API with the root credentials of this one, and be in no group. The first round only adds: nothing is deleted.
siteReplication.name: Name
siteReplication.created: Sites grouped: the first synchronization started.
siteReplication.removeConfirm: Every site reached forgets the group and the bucket replication rules it added. Nothing that was replicated is deleted.

remoteTiers.title: Remote tiers
remoteTiers.subtitle: S3 buckets of other servers that the Transition actions of the bucket lifecycle move the data of old versions to. A transitioned version keeps its metadata here and is read from its tier, transparently.
remoteTiers.none: No remote tier: the lifecycle transitions need one.
remoteTiers.addHint: The name is the storage class the lifecycle transitions name. The remote bucket must exist and be reachable with the credentials (read, write, list and delete); they are stored sealed.
remoteTiers.name: Name
remoteTiers.nameHint: Upper case letters, digits, “-” and “_” (e.g. COLD).
remoteTiers.nameInvalid: Upper case letters, digits, “-” and “_”; STANDARD and REDUCED_REDUNDANCY are reserved.
remoteTiers.removeConfirm: Remove tier {{name}}? A tier that still holds the data of transitioned versions cannot be removed.

clusterMaintenance.title: Maintenance
clusterMaintenance.subtitle: Update the binary of every node, or restart or stop the whole deployment. The node you are connected to runs the job and restarts last; the page follows the job while the nodes restart.
clusterMaintenance.none: No update or coordinated restart has run yet.
clusterMaintenance.unreachable: The node does not answer right now: it is probably restarting. The page keeps trying.
clusterMaintenance.stopped: Stop requested: every node is shutting down, this one last. Start the nodes again (systemctl start nexo, docker compose up…) to bring the deployment back.
clusterMaintenance.rollingHint: One node at a time, each one only while the cluster keeps its write quorum with a node down: no interruption.
clusterMaintenance.allHint: Every node together: a short interruption. Needed to change the major version.
clusterMaintenance.updateTitle: Update the binary of every node
clusterMaintenance.updateHint: Every node downloads the binary next to the one it runs, checks its SHA-256 and its version, then restarts with it. The previous binary is kept as nexo.old.
clusterMaintenance.urlInvalid: Enter the http(s) URL of the binary for the platform of the nodes.
clusterMaintenance.restartHint: The nodes restart in place with the same binary and command line.
clusterMaintenance.stopHint: Every node stops, the one you are connected to last: the deployment and this console go offline until the nodes are started again from their hosts.

clusterExpand.title: Change the pools of the deployment
clusterExpand.addHint: A cluster grows by appending pools: describe each new pool with one argument with ellipses, as on the command line. The existing data stays where it is. Decommissioned pools can be removed in the same change.
clusterExpand.valid: Valid topology: {{pools}} pools on {{nodes}} nodes, as every node will parse it.
clusterExpand.applyHint: The nodes take the new topology only when all of them start with the same command line: update it on every node, old and new, then stop the cluster and start every node again. A short, planned interruption.

checks.prepare: The new nodes run the same Nexo version, with the same root credentials and KMS configuration, empty drives mounted, names resolvable from every node and the port open between all of them.
checks.backup: IAM and configuration are exported (nexoctl admin cluster export).
checks.endpoints: NEXO_ENDPOINTS (or the arguments) is updated on every node, old and new: the running nodes keep the old one until they restart.

clusterExpand.stopHint: Stopping the cluster takes it and this console offline. Then start every node (old and new) with the new command line and check the pools on this page: during the startup the nodes verify that they share the same topology.
clusterExpand.stopped: Stop requested. Start every node (old and new) with the new command line; once the cluster is back, check the pools here and start a rebalance to spread the existing objects over the new pools.

healing.title: Healing
healing.subtitle: Repair the objects that miss copies or have corrupt shards, and follow the healing the cluster does by itself.
healing.unsupported: Healing needs an erasure-coded deployment: a single drive has no copies to rebuild from.

start.title: Start healing
start.hint: Without a bucket the job heals the format of the drives and every bucket; with the objects option it also checks every object.
start.allBuckets: All buckets and the drive format

options.removeHint: Deletes the versions on too few drives to ever be read.

jobs.title: Healing jobs
jobs.empty: No healing job in the last hour.

items.title: Items that needed healing
items.truncated: Only the first 1000 items are listed.

background.title: Background healing
background.hint: The objects written or read while a drive did not answer are repaired by the node that noticed it; replaced drives are repopulated.
background.queues: Background healing queue of the nodes

clusterPools.title: Pool management
clusterPools.subtitle: Decommission a pool to remove it: it takes no new objects and every version of its objects moves to the other pools, verified before the copy in the pool is removed. A rebalance evens out the usage of the pools.
clusterPools.removeHint: A decommission is complete: remove the pool from the command line of every node and restart them.
clusterPools.confirm: Pool {{index}} will take no new objects and every object will move to the other pools, which need enough free space. The decommission can be canceled while it runs; once complete, remove the pool from the command line of every node.
clusterPools.rebalanceHint: Moves objects from the fullest pools to the emptiest ones, e.g. after adding a pool.
